segmentation.text: shall be ridden upon any sidewalk

elements.justification: The definitions table admits 'motorcycle' as the aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle ('every motor vehicle equipped with a seat or saddle for the use of the driver and designed to travel on not more than three wheels in contact with the ground, excluding an electric bicycle, a tractor or a moped'). ru.aggregate is 'membership of a legal aggregate' and is claimed whole, never expanded into ru.motorcycle. Its 'not a stand-in for' clauses do not apply: the words name a class, not a role described by conduct or a relational role. The word 'No' negates the duty the obligation span s3 states.

'Motor scooter' has no applicable definition, so its words are mapped by contract. A scooter driven by a motor is, in the taxonomy the corpus posts, either a moped (DEF-NRS-484A-125: 'a motor-driven scooter, motor-driven cycle or similar vehicle' with a small engine; ru.moped: 'a low-power two- or three-wheeler with a small engine or motor, as a jurisdiction classes it') or an electric scooter (DEF-NRS-484A-082: 'a vehicle with handlebars and an electric motor'; ru.electric_scooter: 'a standing or seated electric scooter with handlebars'). A motor scooter above the moped's power is a motorcycle under DEF-NRS-484A-135 and is carried by s1. The ontology carries no body-style attribute, so a moped of cycle body is read with the scooters the moped definition groups it with. Neither class atom carries a 'not a stand-in for' clause.

'Sidewalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-240: 'that portion of a highway between the curb lines or the lateral lines of a highway and the adjacent property lines intended for the use of pedestrians') is st.sidewalk: 'area for pedestrians between roadway and property line'; its exclusion (not a crosswalk) applies as the definition does: a crosswalk lies across the roadway and is not that portion. 'upon any sidewalk' places the subject on the feature, anchored by rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... sidewalk ...)', for every sidewalk region of the scene. 'ridden' is read through the machine's controlled motion: drv.motion.moving (the road user in motion beyond the speed resolution); a machine standing on the sidewalk is not being ridden.

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city.

applicability: x is a member of the motorcycle aggregate (ru.aggregate=DEF-NRS-484A-135::motorcycle) or carries ru.moped or ru.electric_scooter, and asm.within_city_limits holds.
obligation: Not (drv.motion.moving(x; p.motion_speed_tolerance) and existsRegion st.sidewalk s: rel.occupies(x, s)): at the observation x is not in motion while its footprint overlaps any sidewalk region.

narrowings.why: 'ridden' (who or what rides the machine is not observable) is read through the machine's controlled motion: the machine in motion with its footprint on a sidewalk is ridden there; a machine pushed along the sidewalk is read the same way.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle (ru.motorcycle, an included class of the aggregate) moves along a sidewalk: its footprint overlaps a st.sidewalk region and kin.speed is above the tolerance; asm.within_city_limits is declared true.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same motorcycle moves along the roadway beside the sidewalk; rel.occupies holds for the st.roadway and for no st.sidewalk region; asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A bicycle (ru.bicycle: neither in the motorcycle aggregate nor a moped or electric scooter) is ridden along the sidewalk; asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves beside a sidewalk; the source declares rel.occupies absent, so whether its footprint overlaps the sidewalk is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle stands parked on the sidewalk: kin.speed is zero at every observation; asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A moped (ru.moped) moves along the sidewalk; asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: A motorcycle moves along a sidewalk; asm.within_city_limits is declared false.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

segmentation.text: The following regulations pertain to the
shall be in a counterclockwise direction

elements.justification: The definitions table admits 'vehicle' as DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle ('every device in, upon or by which any person or property is or may be transported or drawn upon a highway', with its exceptions); ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate', claimed whole. It is not a relational role: 'operation' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

'Roundabout' (DEF-LVMC-11-02-130: 'an intersection characterized by a circulatory roadway, channelized approaches and yield control of entering traffic', encompassing 'the area bounded by the outermost curb line') is st.roundabout: 'a rotary intersection: its central island, its circulatory roadway and its entry and exit approaches'; the atom has no 'not a stand-in for' clause, and the defined word keeps its whole extent, approaches and crosswalks included. 'within' places the subject in the feature: rel.occupies, 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'.

'vehicular' is the admitted vehicle aggregate (claimed whole); 'travel' is the vehicle's motion, drv.motion.moving: in motion beyond the speed resolution. A vehicle standing in the roundabout is not travelling.

Counterclockwise travel within a roundabout is travel around its central island (DEF-LVMC-11-02-040: the circulatory roadway is 'used by vehicles to travel counterclockwise around a central island'). drv.motion.clockwise_about_region, called on the roundabout region x occupies, denotes motion clockwise about the region's reference point; the duty is that it does not hold. The concept reads velocity, not heading, so a vehicle backing clockwise around the island is caught, and radial travel on an approach (entering, leaving) has no clockwise component.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate, drv.motion.moving(x; p.motion_speed_tolerance) holds, and existsRegion st.roundabout r: rel.occupies(x, r).
obligation: forallRegion st.roundabout r: rel.occupies(x, r) implies not drv.motion.clockwise_about_region(x, r; p.motion_speed_tolerance). The roundabout is re-bound in the obligation with the same selection (a roundabout region x's footprint overlaps), so each roundabout x is within is the one judged.

narrowings.why: 'operation of vehicles' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; who or what controls it is not observable.

'in a counterclockwise direction' is read as: no motion clockwise about the roundabout's reference point beyond the speed resolution. Radial motion (entering or leaving along an approach) is not clockwise and complies. The roundabout region's reference point (st.region_geometry) is read as the centre the circulatory roadway runs around.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car (an included class of the vehicle aggregate) occupies a st.roundabout region and moves around the central island clockwise: the cross product of its offset from the region's reference point and its kin.velocity is negative with a tangential speed above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car moves around the island counterclockwise within the roundabout region.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car moves along a straight roadway; no st.roundabout region is in the scene.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car occupies a roundabout region and moves clockwise around the island; the source maps the region without its outline and reference point (st.region_geometry absent), so the sense of rotation is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car on the right-hand entry approach inside the roundabout region moves straight toward the island; its tangential component about the reference point is counterclockwise or below the tolerance.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car stands still inside the roundabout region, yielding: kin.speed is zero.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'). 'The driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080: 'every person who drives or is in actual physical control of a vehicle') is a relational role, which ru.aggregate is 'not a stand-in for'; it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion, so the duty binds the vehicle's conduct (agency reading).

'back' is the vehicle moving backwards: drv.motion.backing, its velocity along the direction it points below minus the speed resolution. The concept reads kinematics, not kin.gear, whose contract is 'not a stand-in for: the direction of motion ... backing is read from kinematics'. The places the words name (s3 to s7) are read as conditions of the same observation, so the forbidden act is backing at one of them.

'Intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105: 'the area embraced within the prolongation or connection of the lateral curb lines ... of the roadways of two highways'; the junction of an alley is none) is st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges; a junction where an alley meets another way ... is no intersection'. Its exclusions (not a crosswalk or a stop line) hold: the words name the junction itself. 'into' is the entry: the observation at which rel.occupies(x, i) ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') becomes true (rises).

'Crosswalk' (DEF-NRS-484A-065: the unmarked part at an intersection within the prolonged sidewalk lines, or 'any portion of a highway ... distinctly indicated for pedestrian crossing by lines or other markings') is st.crosswalk: 'marked crossing, or the unmarked prolongation of sidewalks at an intersection', both senses. 'on or over' is the footprint overlapping it at the observation: rel.occupies.

'around' a corner is a path that bends: the vehicle's heading is changing at the observation, drv.motion.turning (yaw-rate magnitude above its resolution). kin.yaw_rate is 'not a stand-in for road curvature'; the concept reads the vehicle's own yaw, not the road.

A street corner is the corner where two streets meet, which lies at the boundary of the intersection region (st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet, bounded by the prolongation of their edges'); a vehicle rounding it overlaps that region (rel.occupies).

assumptions.meaning: The place of the observation lies within the territorial limits of an incorporated city.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and at least one of: (a) existsRegion st.intersection i: rises(rel.occupies(x, i)) - x enters an intersection at this observation; (b) existsRegion st.crosswalk c: rel.occupies(x, c); (c) asm.within_city_limits and drv.motion.turning(x; p.yaw_rate_tolerance) and existsRegion st.intersection j: rel.occupies(x, j) - x rounds a street corner.
obligation: not drv.motion.backing(x; p.motion_speed_tolerance) at the observation.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; who or what controls the vehicle is not observable.

Each place is read at the observation: 'into an intersection' as backing at the observation at which the footprint begins to overlap the intersection (backing further within an intersection already entered is not 'into'); 'on or over a crosswalk' as backing while the footprint overlaps a crosswalk; 'around a street corner' as backing while yawing with the footprint on an intersection inside a city (street: DEF-NRS-484A-265 'every highway inside the territorial limits of a city'). A corner rounded without the footprint touching the intersection region is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car moves backwards (kin.velocity opposite kin.heading) and at this observation its footprint begins to overlap a st.intersection region.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car drives forwards into the intersection.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car backs straight along a roadway mid-block; no intersection or crosswalk is overlapped and it is not yawing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an intersection; the source declares kin.velocity absent, so whether it is backing is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car backs over a marked mid-block st.crosswalk (no intersection).

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: Having entered an intersection forwards, a car backs while yawing round its corner, its footprint on the intersection and on no crosswalk; asm.within_city_limits true.

scenarios.name: branch_3
scenarios.narrative: As branch_2, with asm.within_city_limits false: the corner is no street corner, the car entered forwards and overlaps no crosswalk.

param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
param_proposals.source: Vehicle IMU and tracker yaw-rate noise figures.

segmentation.text: whether or not towing other vehicles
sufficient space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger

elements.justification: The definitions table admits 'motor vehicle' as DEF-NRS-484A-130::motor_vehicle ('every vehicle which is self-propelled but not operated upon rails'); ru.aggregate is claimed whole, never replaced by ru.motor_vehicle, whose own contract says it is 'not a stand-in for: "vehicle" as a legal aggregate'.
'being driven' is the vehicle in controlled motion (agency reading): drv.motion.moving, in motion beyond the speed resolution; the progressive form places the caravan in motion.

'Highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095: 'the entire width between the boundary lines of every way dedicated to a public authority') is st.highway: 'the entire public way between its boundary lines, including sidewalks and shoulders'; its exclusion ('not a stand-in for the roadway') holds, as the words name the whole way. 'upon' anchors the subject: rel.occupies.

'operated to allow ... space between each such vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the space the subject keeps to the vehicle ahead of it in the line, a member of the admitted vehicle aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle or of the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles ('two or more vehicles coupled together'), each claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'): rel.ahead_behind_in_lane ('a is ahead of / behind b in the same lane, along the lane direction') selects that vehicle and rel.surface_gap ('distance between the nearest points of two bodies') measures the space, rather than rel.centre_distance, which is 'not a stand-in for a clearance between bodies'. 'operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency).

operationalizations.standard: sufficient space ... so as to enable any other vehicle or combination of vehicles to enter and occupy such space without danger
operationalizations.convention: Gap-acceptance convention for a merging vehicle: the space must hold the entering design vehicle (the longest combination of vehicles, so that 'any other vehicle or combination' fits) plus an accepted time headway ahead of it and another behind it at the caravan's speed. The bound is p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length plus p.caravan_entry_time_headway times x's kin.speed, the headway term counted once for the gap ahead of the entering vehicle and once for the gap behind it; the bound grows with the speed, so the degree of the speed factor is read. 'each such vehicle or combination of vehicles' is the road user ahead in the lane, a member of the vehicle aggregate or of the combination-of-vehicles aggregate.

assumptions.meaning: The stretch of highway at the observation lies outside every territory classed as a business district.
The motor vehicles of the trace that travel one behind another in the same lane travel together as an organised caravan or motorcade.

residues.why: The words extend the duty to vehicles towing others and to those not towing alike: whether a caravan vehicle tows adds no condition, and a towed unit ahead is already a member of the vehicle or combination-of-vehicles aggregate the obligation reads.

applicability: x is a member of the motor-vehicle aggregate, drv.motion.moving(x; p.motion_speed_tolerance) holds, existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h), and asm.outside_business_district and asm.caravan_or_motorcade hold.
obligation: forallUser y: (not same(x, y) and (ru.aggregate(y, DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle) or ru.aggregate(y, DEF-NRS-484A-050::combination_of_vehicles)) and rel.ahead_behind_in_lane(y, x)) implies rel.surface_gap(x, y) >= p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length + p.caravan_entry_time_headway * kin.speed(x) + p.caravan_entry_time_headway * kin.speed(x). With no road user ahead in the lane the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'operated' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion: the space it keeps to the vehicle ahead in its lane.

'without danger' is read only through the time headway the entering vehicle keeps ahead of and behind it at the subject's speed; the closing speed of the vehicle ahead, the road surface and the sight distance are not read. 'any other vehicle or combination of vehicles' is read through the length of the design combination, the longest an entrant may be.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: Two cars travel one behind the other in the same lane of a highway at cruising speed; asm.caravan_or_motorcade and asm.outside_business_district are true; the follower's rel.surface_gap to the leader is about one car length, below the bound.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with the follower's surface gap well above the design length plus both headways at its speed.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with asm.outside_business_district false (the stretch is in a business district).

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with rel.surface_gap declared absent by the source.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A single car moves on the highway with both assumptions true and no road user ahead of it in its lane: the duty binds it and is met.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with asm.caravan_or_motorcade false.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

param_proposals.name: p.caravan_entry_vehicle_length
param_proposals.convention: Overall length of the longest design combination a highway is designed for (an interstate semitrailer combination), so that any vehicle or combination can occupy the space.
param_proposals.source: AASHTO A Policy on Geometric Design of Highways and Streets, WB-67 design vehicle overall length.

param_proposals.name: p.caravan_entry_time_headway
param_proposals.convention: Minimum accepted lead and lag time gap of a merging or lane-changing vehicle, applied once ahead of and once behind the entering vehicle.
param_proposals.source: Lane-change gap-acceptance studies (critical lead and lag gaps of about one second).

segmentation.text: shall not overtake and pass another vehicle upon the right
when such movement requires driving off the paved portion of the highway

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'). 'The driver' (DEF-NRS-484A-080) is a relational role, which ru.aggregate is 'not a stand-in for'; it is read through the vehicle's controlled motion (agency reading).

'overtake and pass ... upon the right' is drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y): the two heading the same way, side by side, y on x's left, x gaining on y. 'another vehicle' is the admitted vehicle aggregate, claimed whole, for the road user y passed, quantified inside the obligation (a party present only when one is there).

'driving off the paved portion of the highway' is the vehicle's footprint on an unpaved surface of the way: st.shoulder ('the part of the highway beside the roadway not intended for vehicular traffic; paved attribute') with paved false, or st.road_edge ('curb or edge of the roadway; paved attribute for the surface beyond it') whose surface beyond is unpaved and which the footprint straddles; rel.occupies anchors the subject on that feature. Neither atom carries a 'not a stand-in for' clause. 'requires' is read through the conduct: the movement made while off the pavement.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and is off the paved portion: (existsRegion st.shoulder s: rel.occupies(x, s) and the paved attribute of s is false) or (existsRegion st.road_edge e: rel.occupies(x, e) and the paved attribute of e, for the surface beyond it, is false).
obligation: forallUser y: (not same(x, y) and ru.aggregate(y, DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle)) implies not drv.interaction.passing_on_right(x, y; p.same_direction_cos_tolerance, p.motion_speed_tolerance). With no other vehicle beside x the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'The driver' is read through the vehicle's controlled motion; who or what controls the vehicle is not observable.

The pass is judged at each observation of its side-by-side phase in which x, gaining on a vehicle on its left, is off the pavement; 'requires driving off the paved portion' is read through that conduct, so a pass that would have required leaving the pavement but was not made is not read, and an off-pavement position that is neither an unpaved shoulder nor a straddled unpaved edge is not read.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint overlaps an unpaved st.shoulder; a slower car travels the same way in the adjacent lane on its left; their footprints overlap along the subject's heading and the subject is gaining.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car on the unpaved shoulder moves slower than the car beside it on its left: it is being passed, not passing.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car passes a slower car on its right within the paved roadway; no unpaved shoulder or edge is overlapped.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with rel.longitudinal_overlap declared absent, so whether the two are side by side is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car moves alone along the unpaved shoulder; no other road user is in the scene.

param_proposals.name: p.same_direction_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Heading alignment: cosine of the largest angle between two headings still read as the same way of travel (about a quarter of a right angle), covering lane changes and road bends.
param_proposals.source: Lane-change trajectory geometry in naturalistic driving data.

param_proposals.name: p.motion_speed_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Speed resolution: the noise floor of a source's speed estimate, below which a road user is read as standing still.
param_proposals.source: Simulator ground-truth and tracker speed-noise figures (a few tenths of a metre per second).

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
must: Be driven in the right turn lane only
for the purpose of making a right turn

elements.justification: 'a right lane to be used only for turning' is st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', side right. 'single right lane' is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency: 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane', so ordinal equals count) whose left neighbour of the same direction is not itself a right turn lane; st.lane_adjacency is 'not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes', which is not read. 'a highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095) is st.highway, the way x is on (rel.occupies anchors it), and st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on') ties the lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence (status reading).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'); it names a class, not a role.

'Be driven in the right turn lane' is the vehicle's footprint on the lane s1 selects, re-bound with that whole selection: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region') on st.turn_lane side right. The turn the lane serves is made at the intersection the lane runs into: st.lane_enters ('the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'), whose st.intersection region is the target of the declared purpose; st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for the lane a lane leads into', which is not read. 'driven' is read through the vehicle's controlled presence on the road (agency). 'must ... only' makes the purpose (s4) the only case in which the presence is allowed.

intentions.meaning: The road user's current plan includes a right turn at the target region.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h) and existsRegion st.turn_lane L: L's side is right, st.on_way(L, h), L is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency ordinal equals count) and its left neighbour of the same direction is not a right turn lane.
obligation: For every lane L re-bound with the whole selection of the applicability (a right turn lane, single and rightmost, on a highway h x occupies) with rel.occupies(x, L): existsRegion st.intersection i: st.lane_enters(L, i) and intent(int.turn_right, x, i) at the judged observation. Where the source records no intersection L enters, the target is not observed and the verdict is unknown (definedWhen on the existence of the entrance), never violated for want of a record.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' (the lane's legal designation) is read through the marked turn lane's presence on the highway.
'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence in the lane: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven, standing in a queue included.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car's footprint overlaps the single right turn lane of a highway; the source declares int.turn_right false for it at the intersection the lane enters (its plan goes straight on).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with int.turn_right declared true at that intersection.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car drives on a highway with no turn lane on it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car drives beside and possibly within the right turn lane; rel.occupies is declared absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car drives in the through lane beside the single right turn lane; no intention is declared for it.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: The highway has two adjacent right turn lanes (no single right turn lane); a car in the rightmost one has int.turn_right declared false.

segmentation.text: If a highway has been designed to provide a single right lane to be used only for turning
must: While being driven in the right turn lane, not travel through an intersection

elements.justification: 'a right lane to be used only for turning' is st.turn_lane: 'a lane designated only for turning; side ∈ {left, right}', side right. 'single right lane' is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency: 'lane ordinal within the carriageway and the count of lanes in that direction; ordinal 1 is the leftmost lane', so ordinal equals count) whose left neighbour of the same direction is not itself a right turn lane; st.lane_adjacency is 'not a stand-in for the marking between two lanes', which is not read. 'a highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-095) is st.highway, the way x is on (rel.occupies anchors it), and st.on_way ('the public way ... a structure region lies on') ties the lane to that highway. 'has been designed to provide' is read through the lane's presence (status reading).
'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'); it names a class, not a role.

'travel through an intersection' is drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i): x leaves the intersection region with a heading change since its entry below the turn bound, called on the intersection i the right turn lane runs into (st.lane_enters: 'the intersection region a directed approach carrier runs into at its entrance end'; st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet'). 'While being driven in the right turn lane' ties the crossing to the lane: x's footprint overlapped that lane (rel.occupies on the st.turn_lane s1 selects, re-bound) at some observation since its entry into i, that is, it entered i out of the lane. st.lane_enters is 'not a stand-in for the lane a lane leads into' or for x's presence in the intersection, which rel.occupies reads.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h) and existsRegion st.turn_lane L: L's side is right, st.on_way(L, h), L is the rightmost lane of its direction (st.lane_adjacency ordinal equals count) and its left neighbour of the same direction is not a right turn lane.
obligation: Not (existsRegion st.turn_lane L, re-bound with the whole selection of s1 (side right, on a highway, single and rightmost), and existsRegion st.intersection i: st.lane_enters(L, i) and drv.motion.straight_through_region(x, i; p.heading_since_step_carla_scene_graph, p.straight_through_max_heading_change) and rel.occupies(x, L) held at some observation since x's entry into i, the observation at which rel.occupies(x, i) last rose). The act is judged at its recognition, the observation at which x leaves i.

narrowings.why: 'has been designed to provide' (the lane's legal designation) is read through the marked turn lane's presence on the highway.

'travel through' is read as leaving the intersection the lane enters with a heading change since the entry below the turn bound (a straight crossing); 'While being driven in the right turn lane' is read as the footprint overlapping that lane at some observation of the crossing, which it does at the entry made out of the lane. A vehicle in the lane is taken to be driven (agency).

onset.justification: The crossing begins at the entry: the observation at which rel.occupies(x, i) last became true for the intersection i the lane enters.

occasion.recognition: The observation at which x's footprint stops overlapping the intersection it entered, with its heading change since the entry below the turn bound.

under_way.justification: An observation is inside the crossing where it lies from the entry onwards and the heading change since the entry is being integrated from kin.yaw_rate; before the entry nothing is integrated, so the motion read, not the region alone, tells the inside of the act from what precedes it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car in the single right turn lane enters the intersection the lane runs into and leaves it on the far side heading as it entered (heading change since entry below the bound).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car turns right in the intersection and leaves it heading to the right of its entry heading.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A highway without any turn lane; a car crosses an intersection straight.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with kin.yaw_rate declared absent, so the heading change since entry is unknown.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car in the through lane beside the single right turn lane crosses the intersection straight; its footprint never overlapped the turn lane since its entry.

param_proposals.name: p.straight_through_max_heading_change
param_proposals.convention: Turning-movement classification at a junction: a crossing whose net heading change stays below this bound is a through movement, not a turn.
param_proposals.source: Intersection turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

segmentation.text: must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'Every' gives the duty to each member.

'Divided highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section') is a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which a st.median_or_divider region ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies (st.on_way: 'the public way ... a structure region lies on'). 'upon' anchors the subject: rel.occupies on that highway. 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road (agency); the definition's 'constructed so as to impede the conflict of vehicular traffic traveling in opposite directions' is read through the divider's presence (purpose).

'Roadway' (DEF-NRS-484A-220: 'that portion of a highway which is improved and ordinarily used for vehicular traffic, exclusive of the shoulder') is st.roadway, whose contract says 'separate roadways of a divided highway are separate'; it is 'not a stand-in for the sidewalk', not read here. The right-hand roadway is the one on the vehicle's right of the divider, the one whose designated direction is the vehicle's own; the left-hand one is designated for the opposite direction. The duty is read as: on every roadway, or lane of it (st.lane: 'a longitudinal strip of roadway'), lying on the divided highway (st.on_way) that x's footprint overlaps (rel.occupies), x does not point against the designated direction (drv.lane.facing_against_direction). st.lane is 'not a stand-in for a half of the roadway', which is not read.

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h) and existsRegion st.median_or_divider m: st.on_way(m, h).
obligation: forallRegion st.highway h (re-bound: x occupies h and a st.median_or_divider lies on h): forallRegion st.roadway c: (st.on_way(c, h) and rel.occupies(x, c)) implies not drv.lane.facing_against_direction(x, c; p.against_direction_cos_tolerance); and the same for forallRegion st.lane c.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.

'only upon the right-hand roadway' is read as never pointing against the designated direction of a roadway or lane of the divided highway that the vehicle occupies. Crossing a roadway across its direction (at an intersection or a crossover) is not against it; occupying a shoulder is not read; occupying the divider is the duty of NRS_484B_227_1_o2. Where a roadway or lane carries no direction the verdict is unknown.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a highway with a median, a car moves along the left-hand roadway, its kin.heading opposed to that roadway's st.lane_direction (wrong-way driving).

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: The same car moves along the right-hand roadway, its heading along the designated direction.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: On an undivided two-way highway (no st.median_or_divider on it) a car moves in the opposing lane while passing.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with kin.heading declared absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car turning left at an intersection of the divided highway crosses the left-hand roadway across its direction; its heading is never opposed to that roadway's direction.

param_proposals.name: p.against_direction_cos_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which a heading still points against a carrier's designated direction (about half a right angle).
param_proposals.source: Wrong-way-driving detection practice (heading opposed to the lane direction beyond a cone).

segmentation.text: must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'Every' gives the duty to each member.

'Divided highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section') is a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which a st.median_or_divider region ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies (st.on_way: 'the public way ... a structure region lies on'). 'upon' anchors the subject: rel.occupies on that highway. 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road (agency); the definition's 'constructed so as to impede the conflict of vehicular traffic traveling in opposite directions' is read through the divider's presence (purpose).

'any dividing space, barrier or section' is st.median_or_divider: 'physical barrier or dividing section between roadways'. 'driven over, across or within' it is the footprint overlapping it at the observation: rel.occupies ('a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region (... median ...)'), which holds over, across and within alike.

'an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the st.median_or_divider region carrying its 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'; 'through' it is the footprint overlapping that opening region (rel.occupies).

'a crossover' is the divider's opening (st.median_or_divider: 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'); 'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105; on a divided highway 'every crossing of each roadway ... shall be regarded as a separate intersection') is st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet', 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line', neither of which is read. 'at' is the footprint overlapping the opening or the intersection (rel.occupies). 'established by a public authority' is read through the feature's presence (status reading).

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h) and existsRegion st.median_or_divider m: st.on_way(m, h).
obligation: forallRegion st.median_or_divider m: (rel.occupies(x, m) and st.on_way(m, h) for a highway h x occupies) implies (the opening attribute of m holds, or existsRegion st.intersection i: rel.occupies(x, i)).

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.
'established by a public authority' (the legal status of the crossover or intersection) is read through the opening's or the intersection's presence on the road.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: A car drives across a raised median section without an opening, between intersections: its footprint overlaps a st.median_or_divider region whose opening attribute is false, and no intersection.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car moves along the right-hand roadway; its footprint overlaps no median or divider region.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car on an undivided highway (no st.median_or_divider on it) crosses its painted centre line.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: A car moves next to the median; rel.occupies is declared absent.

scenarios.name: branch_1
scenarios.narrative: A car crosses the median through a crossover: its footprint overlaps a median region whose opening attribute is true.

scenarios.name: branch_2
scenarios.narrative: A car turning at an intersection of the divided highway clips the median nose: its footprint overlaps the median and the st.intersection region.

segmentation.text: must be driven only upon the right-hand roadway
and must not be driven over, across or within any dividing space, barrier or section
or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
except through an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space
or at a crossover or intersection established by a public authority

elements.justification: 'vehicle' is the admitted aggregate DEF-NRS-484A-320::vehicle, claimed whole (ru.aggregate: 'membership of a legal aggregate'); 'Every' gives the duty to each member.

'Divided highway' (DEF-NRS-484A-070: 'a highway divided into two or more roadways by means of a physical barrier or dividing section') is a st.highway region ('the entire public way between its boundary lines') on which a st.median_or_divider region ('physical barrier or dividing section between roadways') lies (st.on_way: 'the public way ... a structure region lies on'). 'upon' anchors the subject: rel.occupies on that highway. 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road (agency); the definition's 'constructed so as to impede the conflict of vehicular traffic traveling in opposite directions' is read through the divider's presence (purpose).

The 'must not' of the preceding words governs this list ('must not be driven over ... or make any ...'). 'left turn' is drv.motion.left_turn (heading change to the left over the recognition window, short of a reversal); 'U-turn' (DEF-NRS-484B-077: 'the turning of a vehicle upon a highway so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not') is drv.motion.u_turn; a 'semicircular turn' turns the vehicle through a half circle so that it proceeds the opposite way, a reversal of heading that drv.motion.u_turn recognizes however the turn is made.

'an opening in the barrier or dividing section or space' is the st.median_or_divider region carrying its 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'; 'through' it is the footprint overlapping that opening region (rel.occupies).

'a crossover' is the divider's opening (st.median_or_divider: 'opening attribute where a crossover exists'); 'intersection' (DEF-NRS-484A-105; on a divided highway 'every crossing of each roadway ... shall be regarded as a separate intersection') is st.intersection: 'the region where two roadways meet', 'not a stand-in for a crosswalk or a stop line', neither of which is read. 'at' is the footprint overlapping the opening or the intersection (rel.occupies). 'established by a public authority' is read through the feature's presence (status reading).

applicability: x is a member of the vehicle aggregate and either x occupies a divided highway at the observation (existsRegion st.highway h: rel.occupies(x, h) and existsRegion st.median_or_divider m: st.on_way(m, h)), or it did so at some observation of the window of p.turn_recognition_window behind at which drv.motion.turning(x; p.yaw_rate_tolerance) held (some moment of a turn under way).
obligation: At an observation at which drv.motion.left_turn(x; p.turn_recognition_window, p.left_turn_min_angle, p.reversal_min_angle) or drv.motion.u_turn(x; p.turn_recognition_window, p.reversal_min_angle, p.reversal_max_angle) rises (the act's recognition), the act is excepted only where, at some observation of the window of p.turn_recognition_window behind at which drv.motion.turning(x; p.yaw_rate_tolerance) held, x's footprint overlapped a st.median_or_divider region whose opening attribute holds or a st.intersection region; otherwise violated. At observations at which neither act rises the duty is met.

narrowings.why: 'driven' is read through the vehicle's presence on the road: a vehicle on the road is taken to be driven.
'established by a public authority' (the legal status of the crossover or intersection) is read through the opening's or the intersection's presence on the road.

The turns are recognized over a window of fixed length: a turn or reversal that takes longer than the window is not recognized, and the moments of the act are read as the turning observations of that window, which may include a separate turn made just before.

under_way.words: or make any left turn, semicircular turn or U-turn
under_way.justification: An observation is inside the turn where it lies in the recognition window behind the act's recognition and the vehicle's heading is changing there (drv.motion.turning, its yaw rate above the resolution); observations of the window at which it drives straight, before the turn began, are not inside it.

scenarios.name: forbid
scenarios.narrative: On a divided highway a car makes a U-turn within its right-hand roadway between intersections, nowhere near a median opening: heading reverses within the window; no intersection or opening is overlapped while it turns.

scenarios.name: permit
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight along the right-hand roadway of the divided highway; no turn rises.

scenarios.name: idle
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a U-turn on an undivided highway; it was on no divided highway in the window.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As forbid, with kin.yaw_rate declared absent, so the heading change over the window is unknown.

scenarios.name: occasion_s2
scenarios.narrative: A car begins a left turn on the divided highway mid-block, crossing toward a side driveway without an opening, and completes the turn off the divided highway; it was on the divided highway at turning observations of the window.

scenarios.name: occasion_s2_outside
scenarios.narrative: A car leaves the divided highway onto an undivided road, drives straight on it, then turns left there; at no turning observation of the window was it on the divided highway.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a U-turn through a median opening: at some turning observations its footprint overlaps the median region whose opening attribute holds.

scenarios.name: occasion_s6_outside
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight past and over a median opening region, then later, mid-block, reverses its heading within the roadway; while it turns it overlaps no opening and no intersection.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7
scenarios.narrative: A car turns left at an intersection of the divided highway: its footprint overlaps the st.intersection region at turning observations.

scenarios.name: occasion_s7_outside
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight through an intersection, then mid-block makes a U-turn within the roadway; while it turns it overlaps no intersection and no opening.

param_proposals.name: p.turn_recognition_window
param_proposals.convention: The time within which a turn or a reversal, a reversal made in several moves included, is completed: the window over which the heading change that recognizes it is measured.
param_proposals.source: Intersection turning times and three-point-turn durations in naturalistic driving data.

param_proposals.name: p.left_turn_min_angle
param_proposals.convention: The heading change to the left beyond which a manoeuvre is a turn rather than a lane change or a bend's drift.
param_proposals.source: Turning-movement classification practice in trajectory studies.

param_proposals.name: p.reversal_min_angle
param_proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal); also the upper end of a left turn's band.
param_proposals.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

param_proposals.name: p.reversal_max_angle
param_proposals.convention: The heading change magnitude beyond which the heading has come round past the opposite direction (a loop rather than a reversal).
param_proposals.source: U-turn classification practice in trajectory studies.

param_proposals.name: p.yaw_rate_tolerance
param_proposals.convention: Yaw-rate resolution: the noise floor of a source's yaw-rate estimate, below which a heading is read as not changing.
param_proposals.source: Vehicle IMU and tracker yaw-rate noise figures.

contract: A road user is in motion at the observation: the magnitude of its velocity (kin.speed) exceeds `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution, below which a reading counts as standing still. It denotes motion in any direction, forwards or backwards, whoever or whatever controls the road user. Not denoted: the direction of motion; a halt held over a window, since the concept reads the one observation.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: The source's speed resolution: a speed at or below it counts as standing still.

elements.justification: kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity', m/s; it carries no direction, which the concept does not need.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car's kin.speed is well above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car stands: kin.speed is zero.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.speed absent.

contract: A road user moves backwards at the observation: the component of its velocity (kin.velocity) along the direction it points (kin.heading) is below minus `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution. Not denoted: the gear selected, since a vehicle in reverse gear standing still is not backing and one rolling backwards in a forward gear is; motion across the direction it points, such as a sideways slide; a road user standing still.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: The source's speed resolution: a backward component at or below it in magnitude counts as none.

elements.justification: kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', m/s, world frame; its dot product with the heading is the signed motion along the body's axis.
kin.heading: 'direction the body points', a unit vector read normalised; a zero vector reads unknown.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car's velocity points opposite its heading with a magnitude above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car moves forwards: its velocity points along its heading.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.velocity absent.

contract: A road user's heading is changing at the observation: the magnitude of its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate) exceeds `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's yaw-rate resolution, to either hand and whether the road user moves forwards or backwards. Not denoted: the curvature of the road, which the concept does not read; a completed turn or the angle turned; the hand of the turn.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: The source's yaw-rate resolution: a yaw rate at or below it in magnitude counts as none.

elements.span: the magnitude of its yaw rate (kin.yaw_rate)
elements.justification: kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading', deg/s, signed; its magnitude is turning to either hand. It is 'not a stand-in for road curvature': the concept reads the road user's own yaw.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car rounds a corner with a yaw rate well above the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight: its yaw rate is zero.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The source declares kin.yaw_rate absent.

contract: A road user moves clockwise about a region's reference point at the observation: seen from above in the world frame, in the sense opposite to the one in which the ontology counts a left turn as counter-clockwise, the component of its velocity (kin.velocity) perpendicular to the line from the region's reference point (st.region_geometry) to the road user's reference point (kin.position) points clockwise about the region's reference point, and that component's magnitude exceeds `tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution. It is computed from the cross product c of the offset of the road user's reference point from the region's reference point with the velocity (the offset's first component times the velocity's second, minus the offset's second component times the velocity's first), negative for clockwise motion: the concept holds where c is negative and c times c exceeds tol times tol times the squared length of the offset. Not denoted: the direction the road user points, since a vehicle backing clockwise moves clockwise; motion toward or away from the reference point, such as entering or leaving; whether the road user occupies the region, which the caller states; the designated direction of any carrier.

params.name: tol
params.meaning: The source's speed resolution: a tangential speed at or below it counts as no rotation.

elements.justification: kin.velocity: 'velocity vector', m/s, world frame.
st.region_geometry: 'the reference point and the boundary polygon of a structure region in the world frame'.
kin.position: 'position of the body's reference point', m, world frame.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car circles a roundabout's island clockwise at speed: the cross product is negative and its tangential speed exceeds the tolerance.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: The car circles the island counterclockwise.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: The region is mapped without its reference point (st.region_geometry absent).

contract: Road user a is passing road user b on b's right at the observation: the two head the same way (rel.same_direction with cosine tolerance `cos_tol`), their footprints overlap along a's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative, so the two are side by side), b lies to a's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing from a to b is positive, left positive), and a's speed (kin.speed) exceeds b's by more than `speed_tol`, a tolerance that names only the source's speed resolution. It holds at each observation of the side-by-side phase in which a gains on b. Not denoted: the approach from behind before the footprints overlap, or the moment a draws clear ahead; a pass on b's left; b gaining on a; a lane change; where either road user is, which the caller states.

params.name: cos_tol
params.meaning: Cosine of the largest angle between the two headings still read as the same way.

params.name: speed_tol
params.meaning: The source's speed resolution: a speed difference at or below it counts as none.

elements.span: the two head the same way (rel.same_direction with cosine tolerance `cos_tol`)
elements.justification: rel.same_direction: 'headings aligned: the cosine of the angle between the headings is above its tolerance'.

elements.span: their footprints overlap along a's heading (rel.longitudinal_overlap not negative
elements.justification: rel.longitudinal_overlap: 'the bodies overlap along the subject's heading (side by side)', negative for the gap between the projections.

elements.span: b lies to a's left (the lateral component of rel.bearing from a to b is positive
elements.justification: rel.bearing: 'direction of b from a in a's frame (for "on the right of" ...)'.
kin.speed: 'magnitude of velocity'; with the headings aligned, the faster one gains.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: Car a, on the right of car b and side by side with it, both heading the same way, moves faster than b.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: Car a is side by side with b on b's right but slower than b.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, with rel.longitudinal_overlap declared absent.

contract: A road user has travelled straight through a region, such as an intersection the caller passes: at the observation it leaves the region (its footprint overlaps the region, rel.occupies, at the observation before and not at this one), and the magnitude of its heading change since its entry, the observation at which the overlap last became true, integrated from its yaw rate with sampling step bound `step`, is below `max_angle`, the heading change below which a crossing counts as straight. The act begins at the entry, the observation at which the overlap last became true. The act is recognized at the observation it leaves the region. The concept holds only at the exit observation, ending at the next observation. Conduct before the entry is not read. Not denoted: a turn, a heading change at or beyond `max_angle`; a road user still within the region; which carrier it entered from, which the caller states; a crossing whose entry the recording does not show, for which the heading change since entry is unknown.

params.name: step
params.meaning: The sampling step bound of the heading-change integration: the largest gap between consecutive observations it integrates across.

params.name: max_angle
params.meaning: The heading change since entry below which a crossing counts as straight.

act.onset: The act begins at the entry, the observation at which the overlap last became true.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation it leaves the region.
act.extent: The concept holds only at the exit observation, ending at the next observation.
act.history: Conduct before the entry is not read.

elements.span: its footprint overlaps the region, rel.occupies
elements.justification: rel.occupies: 'a road user's footprint overlaps a lane / region'; its fall is the exit and its last rise the entry.
kin.yaw_rate: 'rate of change of heading, positive when the heading turns to the left'; Term.headingSince integrates it from the entry.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an intersection and leaves it on the far side heading as it entered.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car enters an intersection, turns right and leaves it.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, with kin.yaw_rate declared absent.

contract: A road user points against the designated direction of travel of a carrier at the observation: the cosine of the angle between its heading (kin.heading) and the carrier's designated direction (st.lane_direction), read as the dot product of the two normalised vectors, is below minus `cos_tol`, the cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed that still counts as against. Not denoted: occupancy of the carrier, which the caller states; the direction of motion, since a vehicle pointing against the direction points against it whether it moves forwards or backs; travel across the carrier, with headings near perpendicular to it; a carrier with no designated direction, for which the concept is unknown.

params.name: cos_tol
params.meaning: Cosine of the largest angle off exactly opposed at which a heading still points against the direction.

elements.justification: kin.heading: 'direction the body points', read normalised.

st.lane_direction: 'direction of travel designated for a structure a vehicle travels in — a lane ... or a roadway, one-way roadway or shoulder', read normalised; a place no carrier covers has none (unknown).

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car on a one-way roadway points opposite its designated direction.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car points along the roadway's designated direction.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, with kin.heading declared absent.

contract: A road user has turned to the left: over the window of length `window` behind the observation, its heading changed to the left (prim.heading_change, left positive) by at least `min_angle` and by less than `max_angle`, the change at which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal, not a left turn). The act is recognized at the observation at which the window's heading change entered that band. The act began within the window behind that observation. The concept holds while the window's change stays in the band, and ends when the change leaves it. No conduct before the window is read. Not denoted: a right turn; a reversal of direction; a lane change or a bend's drift below `min_angle`; where the turn is made, which the caller states.

params.name: window
params.meaning: The window over which the heading change is measured: the time within which a turn is completed.

params.name: min_angle
params.meaning: The leftward heading change from which the manoeuvre is a turn.

params.name: max_angle
params.meaning: The leftward heading change from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction (a reversal).

act.onset: The act began within the window behind that observation.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which the window's heading change entered that band.
act.extent: The concept holds while the window's change stays in the band, and ends when the change leaves it.
act.history: No conduct before the window is read.

elements.span: its heading changed to the left (prim.heading_change, left positive)
elements.justification: prim.heading_change: 'the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate; unknown where the window is truncated'.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car turns left at a junction: within the window its heading changes to the left by more than the minimum and well short of a reversal.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car drives straight; its heading change over the window is near zero.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, with kin.yaw_rate declared absent, so prim.heading_change is unknown.

contract: A road user has turned "so as to proceed in the opposite direction, whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not": over the window of length `window` behind the observation, the magnitude of its heading change (prim.heading_change, integrated from its yaw rate across forward and backing moves alike) is at least `min_angle` and at most `max_angle`, the band within which its heading has come round to the opposite direction (a smaller change is a turn, a larger one a loop past the opposite direction). The act is recognized at the observation at which the window's heading change entered that band. The act began within the window behind that observation. The concept holds while the window's change stays in the band, and ends when the change leaves it. No conduct before the window is read. Not denoted: a turn short of a reversal; a loop past the opposite direction; where the turn is made, which the caller states; the class of the road user, which the caller states.

params.name: window
params.meaning: The window over which the heading change is measured: the time within which a reversal, in one move or several, is completed.

params.name: min_angle
params.meaning: The heading change magnitude from which the heading has come round to the opposite direction.

params.name: max_angle
params.meaning: The heading change magnitude beyond which the heading has come round past the opposite direction.

act.onset: The act began within the window behind that observation.
act.recognition: The act is recognized at the observation at which the window's heading change entered that band.
act.extent: The concept holds while the window's change stays in the band, and ends when the change leaves it.
act.history: No conduct before the window is read.

elements.span: the magnitude of its heading change (prim.heading_change
elements.justification: prim.heading_change: 'the signed heading change (degrees, left positive) of a road user over the window behind the observation, integrated from kin.yaw_rate'; integration over forward and backing moves carries 'whether accomplished by one continuous movement or not'.

residues.why: The place of the turn is the caller's condition: the concept reads the road user's motion only.
The class of the road user is the caller's condition, stated with its own admitted aggregate.

scenarios.name: holds
scenarios.narrative: A car makes a three-point turn within the window and ends heading the opposite way.

scenarios.name: fails
scenarios.narrative: A car turns left at a junction; its heading change stays short of a reversal.

scenarios.name: blind
scenarios.narrative: As holds, with kin.yaw_rate declared absent.
